prompt:
Create a clean pixel-art atlas from the supplied reference image. The output must be exactly a 2-by-2 grid of four equally sized 64:35 portrait-eye crops, overall aspect ratio 128:70 (64:35). No gutters, borders, labels, or extra panels. Top-left: same face looking gently LEFT, eyes open. Top-right: same face looking gently RIGHT, eyes open. Bottom-left: same face looking gently LEFT, eyes half-lidded. Bottom-right: same face looking gently RIGHT, eyes half-lidded.

Use the supplied grid as the exact source of identity and anatomy. Preserve this angry expression, the same brow shapes and positions, same eye spacing, face crop, skin/hair colors, and same source eye aperture in each row: open must remain as narrow as the reference open row, half-lidded must remain as narrow as the reference half row. Keep the source's warm olive/golden-brown iris color and compact dark pupils. Move each iris only a very small, natural amount sideways to indicate the gaze (about one native pixel), with both eyes looking in the same requested direction. Keep both irises compact and irregularly stepped like native pixel art, fully inside the existing lid opening; preserve the source lid contours and dark lash/eyelid line. Keep sclera subtle and warm beige/tan, never broad white bands. Highlights should be tiny and muted, no bright white glare.

Keep the exact native pixel-art look with crisp stepped pixels and restrained source palette; do not smooth or vectorize. Do not change the eyebrows, raise or widen the eyes, enlarge or round the iris, recolor eyes, add extra highlights, alter expression, or alter other facial details. The bottom row should only differ by the source half-lid aperture plus the same small left/right iris direction.
